prompt.context_jp: エレベーターの扉が開くと、守屋___廊下の隅に一人立っていて、目が合った瞬間に息をのむのが分かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 守屋___廊下の隅に一人立っていて…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits here.

feedback.correct_en: Keisuke steps out of the elevator and discovers Moriya standing there — she enters the scene as new information, so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame Moriya as an already-established topic, but she's just been spotted. を/に don't mark the one standing.

contrast_examples.en: Moriya was in the hallway. (new discovery)
As for Moriya, she was in the hallway. (she's already the topic)

prompt.context_jp: 友利が親戚ごたごたの事情を初めて打ち明ける場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: うちの母ちゃんの 今の旦那さん___ 階段から転んじゃって…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for introducing this new fact?

feedback.correct_en: Tomori is introducing a brand-new piece of news — his mother's husband fell. New-information subjects of events like this take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that the husband is already the discussion topic, which he isn't. も suggests 'also', with no prior parallel.

contrast_examples.en: Dad fell down. (reporting news)
As for Dad, he's doing fine. (topic comment)

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵が「行かない」と言った直後、圭介が妻に向き直って説得する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貴恵 僕___会いに行くべきだと思う 僕もついてるから
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks Keisuke's own stance.

feedback.correct_en: Keisuke is stating HIS personal opinion in contrast to Takie's refusal. 僕は sets 'I' as the topic/contrastive stance — 'as for me, I think…'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 僕が would sound like identifying who thinks this (exhaustive), as if answering 'who thinks so?' — out of place in gentle persuasion.

contrast_examples.en: I think so (expressing my view).
I'm the one who thinks so (exhaustive — out of place here).

prompt.context_jp: 萌子が貴恵の母について語る場面。「けど」で逆接する前半の主語。
prompt.prompt_jp: 伯母さん___ やりたい放題だったけど 何だかんだ 東京から帰って 伯母さんの面倒みてたし…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up the contrast with the 'けど'?

feedback.correct_en: The けど signals contrast between the aunt's selfish behavior and Takie's devotion. は naturally sets up that contrastive frame on 伯母さん.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 伯母さん as newly introduced subject of a single event, missing the 'on one hand…' nuance that the sentence needs.

contrast_examples.jp: 母は厳しいけど、優しい。
contrast_examples.en: Mother is strict, but kind. (contrastive は)
It's Mother who is strict. (identifying/new info)

prompt.context_jp: 友利が圭介に向かって突き放すように言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 姉ちゃん___死んだときから ずっと抜け殻だったじゃん
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside the 'from the time ___ died' clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative/time-clause like 〜が死んだとき, the subject typically takes が rather than は. The clause supplies new descriptive content modifying 'とき'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 姉ちゃんは would try to make Sis the whole-sentence topic, but she's embedded in a 'when X died' clause here.

contrast_examples.jp: 父が亡くなったとき、僕は十歳だった。
contrast_examples.en: When my father died, I was ten. (subordinate が)
My father has passed away. (main-clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 萌子が過去を振り返り、他のときと「最後だけは違った」と語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貴恵 最後___ 車飛ばして 伯母さんのために 赤いセーター 買いに行ってたな
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits '最後___' here?

feedback.correct_en: '最後は' contrasts the last occasion against all the other times — a classic contrastive-は on a time expression.
feedback.incorrect_en: 最後が would try to identify 'the last time' as a new subject, which doesn't match the still-rolling narrative tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 最後は泣いてしまった。
contrast_examples.en: In the end, I ended up crying. (contrastive time は)

contrast_examples.jp: 最後が一番つらかった。
contrast_examples.en: The last one was the hardest. (identifying が)

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵（万理華の中身）が弟の居場所を言い当てる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 友利が幼い頃から必ず逃げ込む場所___ 一つしかない
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before 一つしかない?

feedback.correct_en: The long noun phrase '逃げ込む場所' is the topic being commented on ('as for the places he hides to…, there's only one'). Topic は is standard before 〜しかない comments.
feedback.incorrect_en: 場所が would mark a new subject rather than frame the topic. The sentence is giving a comment about an already-implied set of hiding places.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が行く場所は一つしかない。
contrast_examples.en: The place he goes is only one. (topic は)
There is a place he goes. (existential が)

prompt.context_jp: 千嘉の告白を受けて圭介が返す言葉。
prompt.prompt_jp: 分かるよ 千嘉さん___ これまで頑張ってきたの
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the subject inside the 'のだ' nominal clause?

feedback.correct_en: The whole clause '千嘉さんが頑張ってきた' is nominalized as the object of 分かる. Embedded subjects before の/こと take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 千嘉さんは would try to make her the top-level topic, but she's actually inside what Keisuke 'understands'.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が努力してきたのを知っている。
contrast_examples.en: I know he has worked hard. (embedded が)
He has worked hard. (main-clause topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 萌子が貴恵の人柄を評する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貴恵___ 世話焼きで心配性だから
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits to describe Takie's personality?

feedback.correct_en: This is a general character description of Takie — a classic topic-comment pattern. 貴恵は… 'As for Takie, she's a worrier…'
feedback.incorrect_en: 貴恵が would sound like identifying 'who is the worrier?', not describing her nature in general.

contrast_examples.en: He is kind. (describing character)
He is the kind one. (identifying — out of place)

prompt.context_jp: 叔母が友利に怒鳴る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 姉ちゃん___ 認知症になってからも ロクに帰ってこずに…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in '〜になってから' clause?

feedback.correct_en: '姉ちゃんが認知症になってから' is a subordinate time clause. Subjects of such subordinate clauses regularly take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 姉ちゃんは would try to topicalize her at main-sentence level, but the complaint's main subject is 友利 (you).

contrast_examples.jp: 母が病気になってから、生活が変わった。
contrast_examples.en: Since Mom got sick, life has changed. (subordinate が)
Mom got sick. (main-clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣が友利を強く非難する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: お父さんに当たらないでよ そっち___ 一緒に来てって 言ったんじゃん
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for an accusing 'YOU are the one who…'?

feedback.correct_en: Mai is pinning blame — 'YOU (and no one else) are the one who said come along.' Exhaustive/identifying が carries that accusing emphasis.
feedback.incorrect_en: そっちは would soften it to a mere topic comment ('as for you…'), losing the pointed 'you're the one who' force.

contrast_examples.en: YOU're the one who said it. (accusing が)
You said it, right? (neutral topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 千嘉が実母について語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私っていう存在に まるで興味___ない人だった
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle goes with the stative predicate ない?

feedback.correct_en: 興味がある/ない is a stative existence pattern — the thing that exists (or doesn't) takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 興味を take-ない would need a transitive verb; 興味は could work contrastively, but here no contrast is set up — just a flat description.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は政治に興味がない。
contrast_examples.en: He has no interest in politics.
I do have a little interest. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣が憧れの相手について父に打ち明ける場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 別に 彼氏じゃないし なんか 留学中の彼女___ いるらしいし
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in the existence clause?

feedback.correct_en: A new piece of information: a girlfriend exists overseas. Existence sentences with いる/ある introduce their subject with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 彼女は would make the girlfriend the topic, implying she's already under discussion — but Mai is first bringing her up.

contrast_examples.en: Apparently he has a girlfriend. (new info)
That girlfriend is studying abroad. (already topic)

prompt.context_jp: 友利が圭介をからかう場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: よかったじゃない 若い子___好かれて キスまでしてもらえて
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the agent of the passive 好かれる?

feedback.correct_en: In the passive 〜に好かれる, the person doing the liking is marked with に. '若い子に好かれて' = 'being liked by a young girl'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 若い子が好かれて would mean she herself is the one being liked (subject). で/と don't mark passive agents.

contrast_examples.en: To be liked by a junior colleague.
The junior gets liked (by someone else).

prompt.context_jp: 叔母が友利を罵倒する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: スマホ___検索しても あんたの名前なんて と～んと出てこねえ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the tool/means?

feedback.correct_en: The smartphone is the tool used to search — instrumental で.
feedback.incorrect_en: スマホに would mark a destination/target of searching, which is odd. を would make the phone the object of the verb.

contrast_examples.en: I looked it up with my smartphone.
I saved it onto my smartphone.

prompt.context_jp: 台所で麻衣が母（萌子）に料理の指示を確認する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: お母さん ニンジン 乱切り___いいの？ 煮物よね
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the manner of cutting?

feedback.correct_en: 乱切り is the manner/style of cutting — 'should I cut it in rangiri style?' Manner takes で.
feedback.incorrect_en: 乱切りに would be the end state of a change (〜にする), e.g. 乱切りにする 'cut it INTO rangiri', which uses a different frame.

contrast_examples.en: Is rangiri-style okay? (manner)
I'll cut it into rangiri. (result state)

prompt.context_jp: 萌子が亡き貴恵の夫への想いを茶化しつつ語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貴恵 圭介さんに ___ だったからなあ
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits the teasing 'she was so into him' tone?

feedback.correct_en: ベタぼれ = head-over-heels in love. It captures the earthy, teasing register the cousin uses about the long-married couple.
feedback.incorrect_en: 片思い implies unrequited — they were married. 一目惚れ is only about first sight. 冷淡 is the opposite feeling.

contrast_examples.en: She's head-over-heels for him.
I have a one-sided crush.

prompt.context_jp: 萌子が、圭介が10年立ち直れずにいた話を受けて。
prompt.prompt_jp: あんまり 落ち込み続けてたら ___ できないでしょう
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits — 'she wouldn't be able to ___ (rest in peace)'?

feedback.correct_en: 成仏する is the set expression for a deceased person 'passing on peacefully' — exactly what Moeko means about Takie's spirit.
feedback.incorrect_en: 安心/納得 are about living people's feelings. 我慢 means endure. None carry the Buddhist 'rest in peace' meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: これじゃ成仏できないよ。
contrast_examples.en: She can't rest in peace like this.
Now I'm relieved. (living person's feeling)

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵（千嘉）が母に会えないと拒む場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 親より先に死んだ身よ 今更 ___ 顔なんてない
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'no face to ___ her'?

feedback.correct_en: 顔を合わせる = to come face-to-face with someone. 合わせる顔がない is the set idiom for 'can't bear to face them (out of shame)'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔を見せる = to show up, 顔を向ける = to turn one's face, 顔を出す = to drop by — none carry the shame-at-reunion idiom.

contrast_examples.en: I can't face them (out of guilt).
I'll go show my face / drop by.

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣が手土産を差し出す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: あの… これ ___ ものですけど
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the humble gift-giving phrase?

feedback.correct_en: つまらないものですが／ですけど is the standard humble set phrase when handing over a gift — literally 'it's a trifling thing, but…'.
feedback.incorrect_en: Praising your own gift (すばらしい/おもしろい/大切な) would sound boastful and break the humility convention.

contrast_examples.jp: つまらないものですが、どうぞ。
contrast_examples.en: It's just a small thing, but please accept it.

contrast_examples.jp: すごいものですが、どうぞ。
contrast_examples.en: It's amazing — please take it. (sounds boastful)

prompt.context_jp: 万理華（貴恵）が友利を叱咤する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ 言ってないで 少しは頑張りなさい！
prompt.prompt_en: Which mimetic word fits scolding tone 'stop ___ complaining'?

feedback.correct_en: うだうだ言う = to grumble/whine on and on. It captures the sister's irritation at Tomori's endless self-pity.
feedback.incorrect_en: すいすい (smoothly), のびのび (relaxedly), ゆったり (leisurely) all have positive or neutral senses, not whiny complaining.

contrast_examples.en: Stop whining.
To live freely and relaxed.

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣が同世代の友達の恋愛観を伝える場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: なんか甘えさせてくれるし ___ んだって
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits the context 'older men make them feel ___'?

feedback.correct_en: 癒やされる 'to be soothed/healed' matches the positive 'they spoil us, we feel comforted' logic Mai is reporting.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other three are negative outcomes that contradict the earlier 甘えさせてくれる praise.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼といると癒やされる。
contrast_examples.en: I feel soothed when I'm with him.
I get tired when I'm with him. (opposite)

prompt.context_jp: 千嘉の母への複雑な想いを圭介がやさしく言い当てる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 悩むのは ___ からでしょ？
prompt.prompt_en: What does Keisuke suggest her hesitation really comes from?

feedback.correct_en: Keisuke gently points out that her inner conflict is proof she still wants to see her mother. 会いたい fits the compassionate reading.
feedback.incorrect_en: If she simply hated or had forgotten her, there'd be no 悩み. 怖い alone misses the longing underneath.

contrast_examples.jp: 悩むのは会いたいからだ。
contrast_examples.en: You're torn because you want to see her.

contrast_examples.jp: 悩まないのは興味がないからだ。
contrast_examples.en: You don't struggle because you don't care.

prompt.context_jp: 叔母が友利の生活ぶりを責めるセリフ。
prompt.prompt_jp: いい年こいて 定職にも就かないで ___ 東京で遊んでるんだろうが！
prompt.prompt_en: Which mimetic adverb fits the scolding 'drifting around'?

feedback.correct_en: フラフラ captures the aimless, directionless living the aunt is condemning — 'drifting around with no purpose'.
feedback.incorrect_en: しっかり/きっちり would mean doing it properly — the opposite. のんびり sounds too peaceful; the aunt is accusing, not describing a relaxed life.

contrast_examples.en: He's drifting around aimlessly.
He's working seriously.

prompt.context_jp: 姉（万理華）が友利を認める瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 分かってるよ 友利は友利 ___ ひとりで頑張ってきたんでしょ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle/suffix completes '友利は友利 ___'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜なりに = 'in one's own (limited) way'. 友利は友利なりに頑張ってきた conveys 'he's done his best in his own way', the tender acknowledgment the moment needs.
feedback.incorrect_en: ばかりで/どころか are negative/contrastive. ながらに is poetic 'while being' and doesn't fit this everyday consolation.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は彼なりに頑張っている。
contrast_examples.en: He's trying hard in his own way.
He does nothing but play around.

prompt.context_jp: 焦った圭介が去ろうとする守屋を引き止める瞬間。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Keisuke's flustered, casual call-out here?

choices.text: ま… 待って 送ってくから
ま… 待って 送らせていただきますので
ま… 待って 送ることをいたしますから

feedback.correct_en: 送ってく (= 送っていく) is the natural spoken contraction a flustered coworker would use in the moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is overly stiff keigo for an awkward hallway chase, and (c) is grammatically clunky, not something a native speaker would say.

contrast_examples.en: I'll walk you to the station. (casual)
I'll see you to the station. (polite — different register)

prompt.context_jp: 友利が圭介親子に頼みごとを切り出す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which casual phrasing sounds most natural for Tomori's hesitant request?

choices.text: 一緒に 田舎に帰ってくんない？
一緒に 田舎に帰ってもらうことは可能ですか？
一緒に 田舎に帰るを頼みたい

feedback.correct_en: 帰ってくんない？ (= 帰ってくれない？) is the natural, slightly whiny casual tone a brother-in-law uses with family.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is business-formal and clashes with the family setting. (c) is ungrammatical — 帰るを頼む mixes a bare dictionary verb with を.

contrast_examples.en: Can you help me out? (casual)

contrast_examples.jp: お手伝いいただけますか。
contrast_examples.en: Could you help me? (formal)

prompt.context_jp: 守屋が告白の翌朝、圭介に静かに付け加える一言。
prompt.prompt_en: Which polite phrasing sounds most natural for Moriya's follow-up?

choices.text: 急ぎませんから 考えてもらえたら うれしいです
急がないから 考えてくれると助かるんですけど
急ぎませんので 考えることをしていただきたい

feedback.correct_en: 考えてもらえたら うれしいです is a soft, polite workplace tone — exactly the balance of restraint and warmth Moriya shows here.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) mixes casual 急がない with 助かる — tonal mismatch for a reserved confession to a senior. (c) is awkward, overly stiff Japanese.

contrast_examples.jp: 考えてもらえたら嬉しいです。
contrast_examples.en: I'd be happy if you'd consider it.
I want you to think about it. (blunt — too direct here)

prompt.context_jp: 手土産を受け取った萌子の反応。
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds most natural when praising a thoughtful gift?

choices.text: 気が利くわね ありがとう
気を利くわね ありがとう
気に利くわね ありがとう

feedback.correct_en: 気が利く is the fixed collocation meaning 'thoughtful / considerate'. The particle is always が in this idiom.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気を利く and 気に利く are not standard forms — the idiom lexicalizes with が. (気を利かせる exists as a separate causative pattern.)

contrast_examples.en: You're a thoughtful person.
He kindly thought ahead for me. (different pattern)
